content_policy: Concise factual paraphrases and original CRA2 annotations with primary-source links; full articles are not mirrored.
rights_status: Sources were freely readable at review. No blanket open-data or redistribution license was verified. Public access is not an unrestricted license.

records.reported_facts: A WAF rule deployment introduced a regular expression with excessive backtracking. CPU exhaustion disrupted HTTP/HTTPS serving. The rule rollout was global, performance tests did not detect the problem, and rollback procedures were slow.
records.reported_recovery: WAF mitigation restored traffic; follow-up work included CPU safeguards, performance tests and staged rule rollouts.
records.review_question_inferred: What performance limits and staged rollout checks cover this rule change?
records.caveats: Historical external incident; not evidence of current health.

records.reported_facts: Network maintenance caused a 43-second partition. Automated database failover moved writes across regions. Divergent writes and application topology assumptions complicated safe failback, prolonging service degradation.
records.reported_recovery: Engineers restored database topology and reconciled writes before completing recovery.
records.review_question_inferred: Will automatic failover preserve application assumptions and allow safe failback during this maintenance?
records.caveats: Retain the report's qualifications about reconciliation; do not infer a comparable SEV label.

records.reported_facts: A legacy-app removal operation received site identifiers instead of app identifiers. An API accepted both types without sufficient warning, and the script deleted entire sites. Restoring interconnected products across many sites required recovery capabilities beyond existing single-site procedures.
records.reported_recovery: Teams restored affected sites from backups and developed parallel restoration tooling.
records.review_question_inferred: How are target type, deletion scope and bulk restoration verified before this maintenance?
records.caveats: The report distinguishes sites from customers; preserve those units. A successful small batch used different inputs from the failing batch.

records.reported_facts: During replication recovery, a database directory was removed from the primary rather than the secondary. Backup failures and recovery limitations prolonged the outage and some database changes were lost. Git repositories and wikis were not affected by the data loss.
records.reported_recovery: The database was restored from an earlier LVM snapshot, with additional restoration work for webhooks.
records.review_question_inferred: How are the target host and recoverability verified before a destructive database operation?
records.caveats: Operational recovery action, not a normal application deployment.

records.reported_facts: An incorrectly entered maintenance parameter removed more capacity than intended. S3 index and placement systems were affected; restart and integrity checks took longer than expected, and dependent services were disrupted.
records.reported_recovery: Subsystems were restored. Follow-up safeguards limited removal speed and protected minimum capacity.
records.review_question_inferred: What prevents an incorrect parameter from removing excessive capacity, and is full restart time tested?
records.caveats: Historical regional incident; not current AWS availability evidence.

records.reported_facts: A valid customer configuration triggered a latent software bug introduced by an earlier deployment. The resulting errors affected much of the network.
records.reported_recovery: Fastly disabled the triggering configuration and deployed a software fix.
records.review_question_inferred: Could a valid configuration activate code paths that were not exercised during the original rollout?
records.caveats: The precise triggering configuration and bug implementation are not fully disclosed.

records.reported_facts: A backbone maintenance command unintentionally disconnected data centers. A defect in command auditing failed to prevent it. DNS route withdrawal and loss of internal access complicated recovery.
records.reported_recovery: Engineers regained access onsite, restored network systems and controlled returning load.
records.review_question_inferred: Will recovery access and DNS remain available if this network change fails?
records.caveats: Incident date is October 4; the detailed report was published October 5.

records.reported_facts: Returning traffic exceeded Transit Gateway scaling speed. Packet loss and resource exhaustion interacted with autoscaling and provisioning problems. Changes rolled back during diagnosis were subsequently ruled out as the cause.
records.reported_recovery: Slack restored provisioning and AWS increased network capacity.
records.review_question_inferred: What evidence distinguishes a change regression from dependency capacity exhaustion?
records.caveats: Useful negative causal example: not a successful-change sample and not a change-caused outage.

records.reported_facts: A database permission change exposed additional metadata rows to a query. Duplicate feature entries produced an oversized configuration file, exceeding a software limit and disrupting proxy operation.
records.reported_recovery: Cloudflare stopped distribution, supplied a known-good file and restarted affected systems.
records.review_question_inferred: Can this permission change alter generated configuration size or content beyond consumer limits?
records.caveats: A permissions change had runtime consequences; do not reduce the mechanism to generic access denial.

records.reported_facts: Cleanup automation sent an empty query flag. The API returned prefixes beyond the intended deletion set, causing route withdrawals and removal of configuration bindings.
records.reported_recovery: Engineers stopped cleanup, restored advertisements and recovered deleted configuration.
records.review_question_inferred: How are empty filters tested and deletion scope bounded before cleanup automation runs?
records.caveats: The introduction and timeline report differing onset times. Preserve that discrepancy rather than invent one exact onset.

records.reported_facts: A quota-policy data change activated a previously unexercised code path. Blank fields triggered crashes, and rapid global replication widened impact. Recovery encountered dependency overload and insufficient randomized backoff.
records.reported_recovery: Google disabled the affected serving path and managed restart load while restoring service.
records.review_question_inferred: Does testing cover later policy activation, and can rollout and restart load be limited by region?
records.caveats: Provider severity and historical impact must not be converted automatically into a prospective CRA2 risk rating.

records.reported_facts: A Redis CPU-reservation change left a pod unschedulable. Subsequent scaling and eviction behavior disrupted service despite a disruption budget, affecting CI processing and GitLab Duo.
records.reported_recovery: Configuration rollback restored Redis; queued work complicated recovery.
records.review_question_inferred: Can the cluster schedule replacement pods with the new reservation, including during eviction or rollout?
records.caveats: GitLab work items may require browser rendering or an API adapter for extraction.

records.reported_facts: A public staging change request documents a claims-verification worker operation and its reviewer, testing, observability and rollback requirements.
records.review_question_inferred: Are the proposed operation, observations and rollback criteria explicit before execution?
records.caveats: A plan is not proof of successful execution and is not a production success label.

records.reported_facts: A safety-filter configuration activated request-dependent code paths that disrupted a shared filtering service. Reduced serving capacity caused overload and elevated 429 and 503 responses.
records.reported_recovery: Google rolled back the configuration and added serving capacity.
records.review_question_inferred: Which request-shape tests and dependency-capacity checks cover this configuration rollout?
records.caveats: Exact configuration and request conditions are undisclosed. Final impact times revise preliminary estimates; do not combine them into a longer outage.

records.original_service: Google Cloud VMware Engine Stretched Clusters
records.reported_facts: A structurally valid network configuration exposed routing defects that dropped selected private-address traffic and disrupted inter-zone connectivity. BGP and BFD checks used unaffected address spaces and remained functional.
records.reported_recovery: Google rolled back configuration, reset network state and rerouted traffic.
records.review_question_inferred: Which probes verify the actual private-address data path when control-plane health checks remain healthy?
records.caveats: Final analysis differs from early BGP-flapping updates and revises the recovery time. Healthy control-plane checks did not establish end-to-end connectivity.

records.reported_facts: Scheduled optical maintenance reduced network capacity. Automatic rerouting failed to use sufficient alternate capacity, causing congestion and packet loss. Shared consensus and metadata dependencies propagated failures to dependent services.
records.reported_recovery: Google drained traffic, restored capacity and gradually reintroduced traffic; backlog and workflow recovery continued afterward.
records.review_question_inferred: How will maintenance preserve alternate-path bandwidth and verify recovery of dependent services?
records.caveats: The final core-impact window differs from dashboard times; product recovery was not simultaneous. Specific circuit changes and rerouting defects are unspecified.

records.original_service: Google Compute Engine and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
records.reported_facts: A router capacity upgrade used incompatible transceivers. Missing sequencing and verification allowed maintenance to disconnect redundant fiber paths, disrupting specific clusters and dependent services.
records.reported_recovery: Google diverted traffic, reinstalled original transceivers and restored connectivity.
records.review_question_inferred: How will compatibility and connectivity be verified before upgrading the next redundant router?
records.caveats: Final analysis and an addendum expand preliminary scope to clusters spanning us-central1-b and us-central1-f, not whole-zone failures. Dashboard and narrative onset differ by one minute.

records.reported_facts: A traffic-sorting configuration bypassed capacity-aware routing and overloaded storage nodes. An incomplete upload-planner rollback allowed recurrence the following day. A separate database issue affected metadata processing.
records.reported_recovery: Google drained traffic and completed the routing rollback. A separate database rollback addressed metadata processing.
records.review_question_inferred: How will rollback validation confirm that every traffic-planning component again respects backend capacity?
records.caveats: October 8 and 9 had distinct impact periods, not continuous downtime. Final onset revises an initial estimate; retain the separate metadata cause.

records.reported_facts: During temporary single-feed maintenance, an external cable fault removed the active supply. Identical generator controllers sensed upstream voltage on an isolated feeder, ignored breaker position and withheld startup. UPS batteries depleted; failover stressed regional dependencies.
records.reported_recovery: Google transferred utility supply, corrected controller checks and gradually restored infrastructure and traffic.
records.review_question_inferred: Do failure tests cover breaker state, shared controller logic and capacity during the temporary maintenance configuration?
records.caveats: Maintenance did not cause the external fault. UTC incident date corresponds to October 19 Pacific. Final timing and product scope revise early updates; recovery exceeded the headline window.
